messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT at 06:44 UTC — Canary deployment 'route_split_v3' is triggering latency SLO breaches in us-west1. p50 ~120ms -> 310ms, p95 850ms -> 2.4s, error rate +0.8%. Auto-page to #eng-oncall :warning:
oncall-alex: I'm on it, joining prod console and tracing. any recent deploys?
sre-maya: seeing a lot of kernel_fallback events on gpu-hosts-gw-3a and kv_cache miss spikes. prefetched keys rate doubled. logs: `/var/log/runtime/kernel.log` shows repeated selector timeouts.
eng-ryan: we promoted route_split_v3 at 06:43 — it changes kernel selector to quant-k for seq>512 and adjusts batching window to 18ms.
oncall-alex: timeline matches. I'm pausing canary traffic to limit blast radius.
incidents-bot: ACTION: paused canary traffic for route_split_v3 (policy: 50% -> 0%) — auto-detected by rollout tracker.
sre-maya: after pause: p95 dropped to ~1.1s but still noisy. Kernel fallback thrash continues, looks like selector oscillation causing micro-batching variance.
eng-ryan: KERNEL selector oscillation known issue when prefetched kv misses spike under quant path. Reverting kernel selector to stable 'baseline-k' for affected hosts.
infra-jen: I'm prepping the configmap change, will patch selector on nodes in the impacted pool.
oncall-alex: if we can flip the feature flag, do that first so traffic routing is safe. Flag name is `route_split_v3_enable`.
eng-ryan: running flag flip now:
```
# flip feature flag
curl -X POST https://config.internal/flags/route_split_v3_enable/off -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# and fallback safety: pin kernel selector
kubectl patch cm runtime-kernel-config -n redwood --patch '{"data":{"selector":"baseline-k"}}'
```
pm-lina: notifying support + CSMs for customers in us-west1. Early estimate: ~4% of requests saw >=1.5s latency, no widespread 5xxs but a few client timeouts reported.
incidents-bot: Flag flip acknowledged, change queued to 3 control-plane instances.
infra-jen: change applied to pool gw-3a and gw-3b. rolling restart of runtime pods to pick config (staggered).
sre-maya: after kernel pin and restarts p95 ~420ms, p99 spikes rare. kv_cache miss rate trending down. Looks like rollback mitigated most of the regression.
oncall-alex: good call. Did we also revert the batching window change?
eng-ryan: not yet. batching window of 18ms kept for a short test, but it amplifies tail variance with selector oscillation. Reverting batching window -> 12ms in the next minute.
incidents-bot: Deploy health: canary paused, selector pinned, batching window reverted. Incident severity -> reduced to SEV3 (SLOs still noisy but stable).
pm-lina: Customer impact note for communications: small subset of customers in US-W had degraded latency 06:43–07:12 UTC, estimated 4% of requests affected, no data exposure. Draft message ready for review.
oncall-alex: handoff: @oncall-ben I'm handing this to you for monitoring through the 08:00 shift. Summary: route_split_v3 caused kernel selector oscillation -> kernel fallback thrash -> increased p95/p99. Actions taken: paused canary, flipped flag off, pinned kernel selector, reverted batching window, rolling restarts. Current status: stable but watching.
oncall-ben: acknowledged, I'll keep eyes on it and run the rollout replay checklist. Please add any runbook links.
eng-ryan: runbook refs: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/kernel-selector and https://internal.redwood/runbooks/rollouts. TODOs: follow-up postmortem, tighten canary criteria for quant path, add auto-safety to avoid selector oscillation (rate limit config changes), instrument KV prefetch throttles.
sre-maya: postmortem item: add alerts for rapid selector-switch counts and KV miss deltas.
pm-lina: scheduling customer follow-up email for impacted accounts, waiting on final metrics from analytics.
oncall-alex: thanks team. adding labels: incident=canary-misalignment, cause=kernel_selector, mitigated_by=flag_flip+pin. :thumbsup:
incidents-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (mitigated) — follow-up assigned to eng-ryan, sre-maya, and infra-jen for detailed postmortem.
oncall-ben: taking over monitoring. will escalate if any regression reappears.
